Alternatively, upon Fiscal Service's request, the creditor agency shall return promptly to the disbursing official an amount equal to the amount of the offset (without regard to whether any other amounts payable to such disbursing official have been paid).
claims.summary: If Fiscal Service learns a payment should not have been made, it must notify the creditor agency. Fiscal Service may deduct the offset amount from future payments. Alternatively, upon request, the creditor agency must return the offset amount to the disbursing official.

claims.quote: (3) Generally, the disbursing official is not responsible for refunding money to debtors. The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service any time the creditor agency returns all or any part of an offset payment to an affected payee. See paragraph (d)(10)(v) of this section. Fiscal Service and the creditor agency shall adjust the debtor records appropriately.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must notify Fiscal Service whenever it returns all or part of an offset payment to an affected payee. Fiscal Service and the creditor agency must adjust debtor records accordingly.

claims.quote: (j) Fees. Fiscal Service may charge a fee sufficient to cover the full cost of implementing the centralized offset program, including the amount of any fees charged by other disbursing officials conducting an offset under this section. Fiscal Service may deduct the fees from amounts collected by offset or may bill the creditor agencies. Fiscal Service will charge fees only for actual offsets collected.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may charge fees to cover the full cost of implementing the centralized offset program. Fees may be deducted from collected amounts or billed to creditor agencies. Fees are only charged for actual offsets collected.

claims.quote: (l) Social Security numbers. Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail. In addition, Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer the Treasury Offset Program, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure Social Security numbers are not visible on the outside of mailed packages. It generally must redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents. However, it may include them in mailed documents for specific purposes such as interoffice communications, notices about offsets, responses to debtor requests, or when required by law.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials of the Federal Government will conduct administrative offset to collect past-due State debts certified to Fiscal Service, and participating States will conduct State payment offset to collect delinquent Federal debts in accordance with the terms of reciprocal agreements entered into between the States and Fiscal Service, acting on behalf of the Secretary.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service and participating States must conduct administrative offset and State payment offset, respectively, to collect delinquent debts in accordance with reciprocal agreements.

claims.quote: Upon notification of a delinquent State debt from a participating State to Fiscal Service, disbursing officials of the United States shall offset the Federal payments specified in the reciprocal agreement to collect the State debt.
claims.affected_party: disbursing officials of the United States
claims.summary: Disbursing officials of the United States must offset Federal payments specified in the reciprocal agreement to collect delinquent State debts.

claims.quote: The amount offset, minus an offset fee, shall be forwarded to the State to be distributed in accordance with applicable laws and procedures.
claims.affected_party: disbursing officials of the United States
claims.summary: The amount offset, minus an offset fee, must be forwarded to the State to be distributed in accordance with applicable laws and procedures.

claims.quote: Upon notification of a delinquent Federal debt from Fiscal Service to a participating State, authorized officials of the participating State shall conduct State payment offset as specified in the applicable reciprocal agreement to collect the Federal debt.
claims.affected_party: authorized officials of the participating State
claims.summary: Authorized officials of the participating State must conduct State payment offset as specified in the applicable reciprocal agreement to collect delinquent Federal debts.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may enter into reciprocal agreements with States for administrative offset and State payment offset. The agreements shall contain any requirements which Fiscal Service considers appropriate to facilitate the offset and prevent duplicative efforts, and shall require States to prescribe procedures governing the collection of delinquent State debts which are substantially similar to requirements imposed on Federal agencies pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(b).
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may enter into reciprocal agreements with States for administrative offset and State payment offset, which must contain requirements to facilitate the offset and prevent duplicative efforts, and require States to prescribe procedures substantially similar to those imposed on Federal agencies.

claims.quote: States may prescribe such procedures through legislation or regulations, as deemed appropriate by State officials.
claims.summary: States may prescribe procedures through legislation or regulations, as deemed appropriate by State officials.

claims.quote: States which have entered into a reciprocal agreement with Fiscal Service pursuant to this section may thereafter request, in the manner prescribed in the reciprocal agreement, that administrative offsets be performed. Such requests shall be made by the appropriate State disbursing official, which, for purposes of this section, means an appropriate official of the State agency that is responsible for collecting the State debt.
claims.summary: States that have entered into a reciprocal agreement with Fiscal Service may request administrative offsets to be performed in the manner prescribed in the reciprocal agreement, with such requests made by the appropriate State disbursing official.

claims.quote: Reciprocal agreements must be signed by a State official authorized to enter into such agreements.
claims.summary: Reciprocal agreements must be signed by a State official authorized to enter into such agreements.

claims.quote: Once Fiscal Service has entered into a reciprocal agreement with a State pursuant to this section, Fiscal Service may request that the State perform State payment offsets to collect delinquent Federal debts in accordance with the terms of the reciprocal agreement.
claims.summary: Once Fiscal Service has entered into a reciprocal agreement with a State, Fiscal Service may request that the State perform State payment offsets to collect delinquent Federal debts in accordance with the terms of the reciprocal agreement.

claims.quote: A duly executed reciprocal agreement is required before a State may request an administrative offset pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(h).
claims.summary: A duly executed reciprocal agreement is required before a State may request an administrative offset pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(h).

claims.quote: A State debt submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset must meet the debt eligibility requirements of 31 CFR 285.5(d)(3)(i).
claims.summary: A State debt submitted to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset must meet the debt eligibility requirements of 31 CFR 285.5(d)(3)(i).

claims.quote: At the time a participating State notifies Fiscal Service of a State debt for purposes of collection by administrative offset under this section, the State shall comply with the certification requirements set forth in paragraph 31 CFR 285.5(d)(6) with the following two exceptions: (i) Paragraph (d)(6)(ii)(E)—Federal salary offset; and (ii) Paragraph (d)(6)(iii)—Federal requirements for the assessment of interest and penalties to Federal debts.
claims.summary: At the time a participating State notifies Fiscal Service of a State debt for purposes of collection by administrative offset, the State shall comply with the certification requirements set forth in paragraph 31 CFR 285.5(d)(6), with the exceptions of Federal salary offset and Federal requirements for the assessment of interest and penalties to Federal debts.

claims.quote: Additionally, with respect to paragraph (d)(6)(ii) of § 285.5, States shall only be required to certify that they have complied with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716 (not 31 U.S.C. 3720A or 26 U.S.C. 6402) and this section 285.6. States shall also certify that they have complied with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure that may be applicable to administrative offset.
claims.summary: With respect to paragraph (d)(6)(ii) of § 285.5, States shall only be required to certify that they have complied with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716 and this section 285.6, and also certify that they have complied with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure that may be applicable to administrative offset.

claims.quote: A State shall be deemed to have complied with the requirements of paragraph (e)(2) of this section with respect to any State debt that the State certified to Treasury for collection pursuant to
claims.summary: A State shall be deemed to have complied with the requirements of paragraph (e)(2) of this section with respect to any State debt that the State certified to Treasury for collection pursuant to.

claims.quote: The Federal payments that will be offset to collect a participating State's debts shall be set forth in the reciprocal agreement.
claims.summary: The Federal payments subject to offset must be set forth in the reciprocal agreement.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials shall conduct administrative offset under this section in the same manner as set forth in 31 CFR 285.5(f) through (i).
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must conduct administrative offset in the same manner as set forth in 31 CFR 285.5(f) through (i).

claims.quote: Neither the Federal disbursing official nor the agency authorizing the Federal payment shall be liable to a debtor for the amount of the administrative offset on the basis that the underlying obligation, represented by the payment before the administrative offset was taken, was not satisfied.
claims.affected_party: Federal disbursing official and agency authorizing the Federal payment
claims.summary: The Federal disbursing official and the agency authorizing the Federal payment shall not be liable to a debtor for the amount of the administrative offset if the underlying obligation was not satisfied.

claims.quote: A State may set forth in the reciprocal agreement the requirements for Fiscal Service to follow when submitting a Federal debt for collection by State payment offset. Such agreements shall set forth all requirements contained in State law for the State payment offset.
claims.summary: A State may set forth in the reciprocal agreement the requirements for Fiscal Service to follow when submitting a Federal debt for collection by State payment offset, including all requirements contained in State law for the State payment offset.

claims.quote: (2) Fiscal Service shall certify to a participating State that each debt Fiscal Service submits for State payment offset has been certified by the Federal creditor agency to be delinquent, valid, and legally enforceable in the amount stated, and that the Federal creditor agency owed the debt has complied with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) prior to submitting the debt for offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must certify to a participating State that each debt submitted for State payment offset is delinquent, valid, and legally enforceable, and that the Federal creditor agency has complied with 31 U.S.C. 3716(a).

claims.quote: (1) An official of a participating State shall conduct State payment offset pursuant to the laws and regulations of the participating State; provided that: (i) If a payment is owed jointly to more than one payee, the entire payment shall be offset for a debt of either payee, unless otherwise prohibited by law or regulation; and (ii) If a payment is made to a person solely in that person's capacity as a representative payee for another person having the beneficial interest in the payment, the disbursing official shall offset that payment only to collect debts owed by the person having the beneficial interest in the payment.
claims.affected_party: An official of a participating State
claims.summary: An official of a participating State must conduct State payment offset according to the laws and regulations of the participating State, with specific provisions for joint payments and representative payees.

claims.quote: (3) An official of the participating State shall notify the payee of the State payment offset. The reciprocal agreement may contain detailed guidance and procedures regarding sending such notice, but shall, at a minimum require that the notice inform the payee of: (i) The type and amount of the payment that was offset; (ii) The identity of the Federal agency that requested the offset; and (iii) A contact point within the Federal agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.affected_party: An official of the participating State
claims.summary: An official of the participating State must notify the payee of the State payment offset, with the notice requiring to inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment offset, the identity of the Federal agency that requested the offset, and a contact point within the Federal agency.

claims.quote: (l) Limitations. A debt properly submitted to Fiscal Service or the State for administrative offset or State payment offset shall remain subject to collection until withdrawn by the entity that submitted the debt for collection, provided the debt remains past-due and legally enforceable for purposes of administrative offset or State payment offset, as applicable. A debt which has been reduced to a judgment shall remain legally enforceable for purposes of administrative offset and State payment offset for as long as the judgment remains enforceable against the debtor.
claims.affected_party: Entity that submitted the debt for collection
claims.summary: A debt properly submitted for administrative offset or State payment offset remains subject to collection until withdrawn by the entity that submitted the debt, provided the debt remains past-due and legally enforceable. A debt reduced to a judgment remains legally enforceable for as long as the judgment is enforceable against the debtor.

claims.quote: (m) Fees. Fiscal Service shall deduct a fee from each administrative offset and State payment offset amount before transferring the balance of the offset funds to the State or Federal agency owed the debt. Pursuant to 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(4), the fee will be in an amount that Fiscal Service has determined to be sufficient to reimburse Fiscal Service for the full cost of the offset procedure. Fiscal Service will notify the States and creditor agencies, annually and in advance, of the amount of the fee Fiscal Service will charge for each offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must deduct a fee from each administrative offset and State payment offset amount before transferring the balance of the offset funds to the State or Federal agency owed the debt. Fiscal Service must notify the States and creditor agencies annually and in advance of the fee amount.

claims.quote: (n) Social Security numbers. Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail. In addition, Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer administrative offset, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure that an individual's Social Security number is not visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail and generally redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents sent by mail. However, Fiscal Service may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents for specific purposes such as interoffice communications, notices about offsets, responses to requests for records, and when required by law.

claims.quote: This section implements the requirement under 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1) that all Federal agencies, using a process known as centralized salary offset computer matching, identify Federal employees who owe delinquent nontax debt to the United States.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must identify Federal employees who owe delinquent nontax debt to the United States using centralized salary offset computer matching.

claims.quote: This section specifies the delinquent debt records and Federal employee records that must be included in the salary offset matching process.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must include delinquent debt records and Federal employee records in the salary offset matching process.

claims.quote: This section establishes an interagency consortium to implement centralized salary offset computer matching on a government-wide basis as required under 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1).
claims.summary: Federal agencies must participate in an interagency consortium to implement centralized salary offset computer matching on a government-wide basis.

claims.quote: Agencies that submit their debt to Fiscal Service for purposes of administrative offset are not required to submit duplicate information for purposes of centralized salary offset computer matching under 5 U.S.C. 5514 and this section.
claims.summary: Federal agencies that submit their debt to Fiscal Service for administrative offset are not required to submit duplicate information for centralized salary offset computer matching.

claims.quote: The receipt of collections from salary offsets does not preclude a creditor agency from pursuing other debt collection remedies, including the offset of other Federal payments to satisfy delinquent nontax debt owed to the United States.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies may pursue other debt collection remedies, including the offset of other Federal payments, to satisfy delinquent nontax debt owed to the United States.

claims.quote: This section does not govern the centralized offset of final salary payments or lump-sum payments made to employees who have left an agency's employ. The centralized offset of such payments is governed by § 285.5 of this part.
claims.summary: The centralized offset of final salary payments or lump-sum payments made to employees who have left an agency's employ is governed by § 285.5 of this part.

claims.quote: (1) As required under 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1), creditor agencies shall participate at least annually in centralized salary offset computer matching.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must participate at least annually in centralized salary offset computer matching.

claims.quote: By notifying Fiscal Service of all past-due, legally enforceable debts delinquent for more than 120 days for purposes of 31 U.S.C. 3716(c)(6), creditor agencies shall have met the requirement set forth in 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1).
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must notify Fiscal Service of all past-due, legally enforceable debts delinquent for more than 120 days to meet the requirement under 5 U.S.C. 5514(a)(1).

claims.quote: (2) Prior to submitting debts to Fiscal Service for purposes of administrative offset (including salary offset) and centralized salary offset computer matching, Federal agencies shall prescribe regulations in accordance with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716 (administrative offset) and 5 U.S.C. 5514 (salary offset).
claims.summary: Federal agencies must prescribe regulations in accordance with the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716 and 5 U.S.C. 5514 prior to submitting debts to Fiscal Service for administrative offset and centralized salary offset computer matching.

claims.quote: (3) Prior to submitting a debt to Fiscal Service for purposes of collection by administrative offset, including salary offset, creditor agencies shall provide written certification to Fiscal Service that: (i) The debt is past-due and legally enforceable in the amount submitted to Fiscal Service and that the creditor agency will ensure that collections (other than collections through offset) are properly credited to the debt;
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must provide written certification to Fiscal Service that the debt is past-due and legally enforceable, and that collections (other than through offset) are properly credited to the debt.

claims.quote: (ii) The creditor agency has complied with the provisions of 31 U.S.C.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must comply with the provisions of 31 U.S.C. (specific provisions not fully quoted).

claims.quote: The creditor agency has complied with the provisions of 5 U.S.C. 5514 (salary offset) and related regulations including, but not limited to, the provisions requiring that the creditor agency provide the debtor with applicable notices and opportunities for a hearing.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must comply with 5 U.S.C. 5514 and related regulations, including providing the debtor with applicable notices and opportunities for a hearing.

claims.quote: The creditor agency is not required to submit the certification set forth in paragraph (d)(3)(iii) of this section prior to submitting a debt to Fiscal Service. However, if the creditor agency does not provide such certification initially, the creditor agency shall provide the Federal employee with the notices and opportunity for a hearing, as required by 5 U.S.C. 5514 and applicable regulations, and shall make the necessary certification before the disbursing official offsets a salary payment pursuant to this section.
claims.summary: If the creditor agency does not provide the certification initially, it must provide the Federal employee with notices and an opportunity for a hearing, as required by 5 U.S.C. 5514 and applicable regulations, and make the necessary certification before offsetting a salary payment.

claims.quote: The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service immediately of any payments credited by the creditor agency to the debtor's account, other than credits for amounts collected by offset, after submission of the debt to Fiscal Service. The creditor agency also shall notify Fiscal Service immediately of any change in the status of the legal enforceability of the debt, for example, if the creditor agency receives notice that the debtor has filed for bankruptcy protection.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must notify Fiscal Service immediately of any payments credited to the debtor's account (other than credits for amounts collected by offset) and any changes in the legal enforceability of the debt, such as if the debtor files for bankruptcy protection.

claims.quote: Creditor agencies may submit nontax debts to Fiscal Service for collection by centralized salary offset irrespective of the amount of time the debt has been outstanding. Accordingly, all nontax debts, including debts that were outstanding for ten years or longer prior to June 11, 2009, may be collected by centralized salary offset.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies may submit nontax debts to Fiscal Service for collection by centralized salary offset regardless of how long the debt has been outstanding, including debts that were outstanding for ten years or longer prior to June 11, 2009.

claims.quote: For debts that were outstanding more than ten years on or before June 11, 2009, creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the notice described in paragraph (d)(3)(ii) of this section was sent to the debtor after the debt was outstanding for ten years.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the notice described in paragraph (d)(3)(ii) of this section was sent to the debtor after the debt was outstanding for ten years for debts that were outstanding more than ten years on or before June 11, 2009.

claims.quote: The creditor agency will provide certification in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (d)(3)(iii) of this section.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide certification in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (d)(3)(iii) of this section.

claims.quote: the disbursing official shall offset the Federal employee's salary payment to satisfy, in whole or part, the debt owed by the employee.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must offset the Federal employee's salary payment to satisfy the debt owed by the employee.

claims.quote: Alternatively, the paying agency, on behalf of the disbursing official, may deduct the amount of the offset from an employee's disposable pay before the employee's salary payment is certified to a disbursing official for disbursement.
claims.summary: The paying agency may deduct the amount of the offset from an employee's disposable pay before the salary payment is certified to the disbursing official.

claims.quote: The salary paying agency shall use such records as it deems necessary to accurately calculate disposable pay in accordance with 5 CFR 550.1103.
claims.summary: The salary paying agency must use necessary records to accurately calculate disposable pay in accordance with 5 CFR 550.1103.

claims.quote: The amount offset from a salary payment under this section shall be the lesser of: (i) The amount of the debt, including any interest, penalties and administrative costs; or (ii) An amount up to 15% of the debtor's disposable pay.
claims.summary: The amount offset from a salary payment must be the lesser of the debt amount (including interest, penalties, and administrative costs) or 15% of the debtor's disposable pay.

claims.quote: Offsets will continue until the debt, including any interest, penalties, and costs, is paid in full or otherwise resolved to the satisfaction of the creditor agency.
claims.summary: Offsets will continue until the debt, including interest, penalties, and costs, is paid in full or resolved to the satisfaction of the creditor agency.

claims.quote: A levy pursuant to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 shall take precedence over other deductions under this section.
claims.summary: A levy under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 must take precedence over other deductions under this section.

claims.quote: When a salary payment may be reduced to collect more than one debt, amounts offset under this section will be applied to a debt only after amounts have been applied to satisfy past-due support debts being collected by the State pursuant to Section 464 of the Social Security Act.
claims.summary: Amounts offset under this section must be applied to a debt only after past-due support debts collected by the State under Section 464 of the Social Security Act are satisfied.

claims.quote: Before offsetting a salary payment, the disbursing official, or the paying agency on behalf of the disbursing official, shall notify the Federal employee in writing of the date deductions from salary will commence and of the amount of such deductions.
claims.summary: The disbursing official or paying agency must notify the Federal employee in writing of the date deductions will commence and the amount of deductions.

claims.quote: When an offset occurs under this section, the disbursing official, or the paying agency on behalf of the disbursing official, shall notify the Federal employee in writing that an offset has occurred including: (A) A description of the payment and the amount of offset taken; (B) The identity of the creditor agency requesting the offset; and, (C) A contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.summary: The disbursing official or paying agency must notify the Federal employee in writing that an offset has occurred, including a description of the payment, the creditor agency, and a contact point.

claims.quote: The disbursing official will advise each creditor agency of the names, mailing addresses, and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due, legally enforceable debt were collected and of the amounts collected from each debtor for that agency.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must advise each creditor agency of the names, addresses, taxpayer numbers, and amounts collected from debtors for past-due, legally enforceable debts.

claims.quote: Agencies that perform centralized salary offset computer matching services may charge a fee sufficient to cover the full cost for such services. In addition, Fiscal Service, or a paying agency acting on behalf of Fiscal Service, may charge a fee sufficient to cover the full cost of implementing the administrative offset program. Fiscal Service may deduct the fees from amounts collected by offset or may bill the creditor agencies. Fees charged for offset shall be based on actual administrative offsets completed.
claims.summary: Agencies performing centralized salary offset services may charge fees to cover costs. Fiscal Service may deduct fees from collected amounts or bill creditor agencies. Fees must be based on actual administrative offsets completed.

claims.quote: The disbursing official conducting the offset will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (j) of this section, to the appropriate creditor agency.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (j), to the appropriate creditor agency.

claims.quote: If an erroneous offset payment is made to a creditor agency, the disbursing official will notify the creditor agency that an erroneous offset payment has been made. The disbursing official may deduct the amount of the erroneous offset payment from future amounts payable to the creditor agency.
claims.summary: The disbursing official must notify the creditor agency of an erroneous offset payment and may deduct the amount from future payments to the creditor agency.

claims.quote: Alternatively, upon the disbursing official's request, the creditor agency shall return promptly to the disbursing official or the affected payee an amount equal to the amount of the erroneous payment (without regard to whether any other amounts payable to such agency have been paid).
claims.summary: The creditor agency must return the erroneous payment promptly upon the disbursing official's request.

claims.quote: The disbursing official and the creditor agency shall adjust the debtor records appropriately.
claims.summary: The disburs,ing official and creditor agency must adjust debtor records appropriately.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will offset tax refunds to collect debt under this section in accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(e) and (f) and this section.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must offset tax refunds to collect debt in accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(e), (f), and this section.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will compare tax refund payment records, as certified by the IRS, with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service. A match will occur when the taxpayer identifying number (as that term is used in 26 U.S.C. 6109) and name on a payment certification record are the same as the taxpayer identifying number and name (or derivative of the name) on a delinquent debt record. When a match occurs and all other requirements for tax refund offset have been met, Fiscal Service will reduce the amount of any tax refund payment payable to a debtor by the amount of any past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligation or unemployment compensation debt owed by the debtor.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must compare tax refund payment records with debt records and reduce tax refund payments when a match occurs and all requirements are met.

claims.quote: Any amounts not offset will be paid to the payee(s) listed in the payment certification record.
claims.summary: Amounts not offset must be paid to the payee(s) listed in the payment certification record.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will only offset a tax refund payment for a State income tax obligation if the address shown on the Federal tax return for the taxable year of the overpayment is an address within the State seeking the offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must only offset a tax refund payment for a State income tax obligation if the address shown on the Federal tax return is within the State seeking the offset.

claims.quote: States shall notify Fiscal Service of debts in the manner and format prescribed by Fiscal Service.
claims.summary: States must notify Fiscal Service of debts in the manner and format prescribed by Fiscal Service.

claims.quote: The notification of liability must be accompanied by a certification that the debt is past due and legally enforceable and that the State has complied with the requirements contained in paragraph (c)(3) of this section and with all Federal or State requirements applicable to the collection of debts under this section.
claims.summary: The notification of liability must be accompanied by a certification that the debt is past due and legally enforceable and that the State has complied with all applicable requirements.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may reject a notification that does not comply with the requirements of this section.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may reject a notification that does not comply with the requirements of this section.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service only will accept notification of past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligations of $25 or more or such higher amounts as determined by Fiscal Service.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will only accept notification of past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligations of $25 or more.

claims.quote: The State is required to provide a written notification to the debtor informing the debtor that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: The State is required to provide a written notification to the debtor informing the debtor that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by tax refund offset.

claims.quote: The notice must give the debtor at least 60 days to present evidence, in accordance with procedures established by the State, that all or part of the debt is not past due or not legally enforceable, or, in the case of a covered unemployment compensation debt, the debt is not due to fraud or the debtor's failure to report earnings.
claims.summary: The notice must give the debtor at least 60 days to present evidence that all or part of the debt is not past due or not legally enforceable.

claims.quote: The State must, in accordance with procedures established by the State, consider any evidence presented by a debtor in response to the notice described in paragraph (c)(3)(i) of this section and determine whether an amount of such debt is past due and legally enforceable and, in the case of a covered unemployment compensation debt, the debt is due to fraud or the debtor's failure to report earnings.
claims.summary: The State must consider any evidence presented by a debtor in response to the notice and determine whether the debt is past due and legally enforceable.

claims.quote: Prior to submitting a debt to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset the State must make reasonable efforts to collect the debt.
claims.summary: Prior to submitting a debt to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset, the State must make reasonable efforts to collect the debt.

claims.quote: The State shall, in the manner and in the time frames provided by Fiscal Service, notify Fiscal Service of any deletion or decrease in the amount of past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligation or unemployment compensation debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: The State must notify Fiscal Service of any deletion or decrease in the amount of past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligation or unemployment compensation debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset.

claims.quote: The State may notify Fiscal Service of any increases in the amount of the debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset provided that the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (c)(3) of this section with regard to those debts.
claims.summary: The State may notify Fiscal Service of any increases in the amount of the debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset provided that the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (c)(3) of this section with regard to those debts.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service shall notify the debtor in writing of: (i) The amount and date of the offset and that the purpose of the offset was to satisfy a past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligation or unemployment compensation debt; (ii) The State to which this amount has been paid or credited; and (iii) A contact point within the State that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service shall notify the debtor in writing of the amount and date of the offset, the purpose of the offset, the State to which the amount has been paid or credited, and a contact point within the State that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will advise States of the names, mailing addresses, and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of State income tax obligations or unemployment compensation debts were collected, and of the amounts collected from each debtor through tax refund offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will advise States of the names, mailing addresses, and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of State income tax obligations or unemployment compensation debts were collected, and of the amounts collected from each debtor through tax refund offset.

claims.quote: At least weekly, Fiscal Service will notify the IRS of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts owed for past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligations or unemployment compensation debts were collected from tax refund offsets and the amounts collected from each debtor.
claims.summary: At least weekly, Fiscal Service will notify the IRS of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts owed for past-due, legally enforceable State income tax obligations or unemployment compensation debts were collected from tax refund offsets and the amounts collected from each debtor.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (h) of this section, to the appropriate State.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (h) of this section, to the appropriate State.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will notify the appropriate State that an erroneous offset payment has been made.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify the appropriate State that an erroneous offset payment has been made.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may deduct the amount of the erroneous offset payment from future amounts payable to the State.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may deduct the amount of the erroneous offset payment from future amounts payable to the State.

claims.quote: Upon Fiscal Service' request, the State shall return promptly to the affected taxpayer or Fiscal Service an amount equal to the amount of the erroneous payment (unless the State previously has paid such amounts, or any portion of such amounts, to the affected taxpayer).
claims.summary: The State shall return promptly to the affected taxpayer or Fiscal Service an amount equal to the amount of the erroneous payment.

claims.quote: States shall notify Fiscal Service any time a State returns an erroneous offset payment to an affected taxpayer.
claims.summary: States must notify Fiscal Service any time a State returns an erroneous offset payment to an affected taxpayer.

claims.quote: The State will pay a fee to Fiscal Service to cover the full cost of offsets taken.
claims.summary: The State must pay a fee to Fiscal Service to cover the full cost of offsets taken.

claims.quote: Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program is permitted to the extent necessary in establishing appropriate agency records, locating any person with respect to whom a reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(e) or (f) is sought for purposes of collecting the debt, and in the defense of any litigation or administrative procedure ensuing from a reduction made under section 6402(e) or (f).
claims.summary: Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program is permitted to the extent necessary in establishing appropriate agency records, locating any person with respect to whom a reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(e) or (f) is sought for purposes of collecting the debt, and in the defense of any litigation or administrative procedure ensuing from a reduction made under section 6402(e) or (f).

claims.quote: (4) The receipt of payments pursuant to this section does not preclude a Federal agency from pursuing other debt collection remedies, including the offset of Federal payments to satisfy delinquent nontax debt owed to the United States. A Federal agency may pursue such debt collection remedies separately or in conjunction with administrative wage garnishment.
claims.summary: A Federal agency may pursue debt collection remedies separately or in conjunction with administrative wage garnishment.

claims.quote: (6) Nothing in this section requires agencies to duplicate notices or administrative proceedings required by contract or other laws or regulations.
claims.summary: Agencies are not required to duplicate notices or administrative proceedings required by contract or other laws or regulations.

claims.quote: Whenever an agency determines that a delinquent debt is owed by an individual, the agency may initiate proceedings administratively to garnish the wages of the delinquent debtor.
claims.summary: The agency may initiate proceedings to garnish the wages of a delin,quent debtor.

claims.quote: At least 30 days before the initiation of garnishment proceedings, the agency shall mail, by first class mail, to the debtor's last known address a written notice informing the debtor of: (i) The nature and amount of the debt; (ii) The intention of the agency to initiate proceedings to collect the debt through deductions from pay until the debt and all accumulated interest, penalties and administrative costs are paid in full; and (iii) An explanation of the debtor's rights, including those set forth in paragraph (e)(2) of this section, and the time frame within which the debtor may exercise his or her rights.
claims.summary: The agency shall mail a written notice to the debtor's last known address at least 30 days before initiating garnishment proceedings.

claims.quote: The debtor shall be afforded the opportunity: (i) To inspect and copy agency records related to the debt; (ii) To enter into a written repayment agreement with the agency under terms agreeable to the agency; and (iii) For a hearing in accordance with paragraph (f) of this section concerning the existence or the amount of the debt or the terms of the proposed repayment schedule under the garnishment order.
claims.summary: The debtor shall be afforded the opportunity to inspect and copy agency records, enter into a written repayment agreement, and request a hearing.

claims.quote: The agency will retain evidence of service indicating the date of mailing of the notice.
claims.summary: The agency must retain evidence of service indicating the date of mailing of the notice.

claims.quote: Agencies shall prescribe regulations for the conduct of administrative wage garnishment hearings consistent with this section or shall adopt this section without change by reference.
claims.summary: Agencies must prescribe regulations for administrative wage garnishment hearings consistent with this section or adopt it without change.

claims.quote: The agency shall provide a hearing, which at the agency's option may be oral or written, if the debtor submits a written request for a hearing concerning the existence or amount of the debt or the terms of the repayment schedule (for repayment schedules established other than by written agreement under paragraph (e)(2)(ii)) of this section.
claims.summary: The agency must provide a hearing, which may be oral or written, if the debtor submits a written request for a hearing.

claims.quote: For purposes of this section, whenever an agency is required to afford a debtor a hearing, the agency shall provide the debtor with a reasonable opportunity for an oral hearing when the agency determines that the issues in dispute cannot be resolved by review of the documentary evidence, for example, when the validity of the claim turns on the issue of credibility or veracity.
claims.summary: The agency must provide the debtor with a reasonable opportunity for an oral hearing if the issues in dispute cannot be resolved by documentary evidence.

claims.quote: If the agency determines that an oral hearing is appropriate, the time and location of the hearing shall be established by the agency. An oral hearing may, at the debtor's option, be conducted either in-person or by telephone conference. All travel expenses incurred by the debtor in connection with an in-person hearing will be borne by the debtor. All telephonic charges incurred during the hearing will be the responsibility of the agency.
claims.summary: The agency must establish the time and location of an oral hearing and bear the responsibility for telephonic charges during the hearing.

claims.quote: In those cases when an oral hearing is not required by this section, an agency shall nevertheless accord the debtor a “paper hearing,” that is, an agency will decide the issues in dispute based upon a review of the written record. The agency will establish a reasonable deadline for the submission of evidence.
claims.summary: The agency must provide a 'paper hearing' by reviewing the written record and establish a reasonable deadline for the submission of evidence.

claims.quote: if the debtor's written request is received by the agency on or before the 15th business day following the mailing of the notice described in paragraph (e)(1) of this section, the agency shall not issue a withholding order under paragraph (g) of this section until the debtor has been provided the requested hearing and a decision in accordance with paragraphs (f)(10) and (f)(11) of this section has been rendered.
claims.summary: The agency shall not issue a withholding order until the debtor has been provided the requested hearing and a decision has been rendered.

claims.quote: If the debtor's written request is received by the agency after the 15th business day following the mailing of the notice described in paragraph (e)(1) of this section, the agency shall provide a hearing to the debtor.
claims.summary: The agency shall provide a hearing to the debtor if the request is received after the 15th business day.

claims.quote: The hearing official shall notify the debtor of: (i) The date and time of a telephonic hearing; (ii) The date, time, and location of an in-person oral hearing; or (iii) The deadline for the submission of evidence for a written hearing.
claims.summary: The hearing official shall notify the debtor of the date and time of a telephonic hearing, the date, time, and location of an in-person oral hearing, or the deadline for the submission of evidence for a written hearing.

claims.quote: The hearing official must maintain a summary record of any hearing provided under this section.
claims.summary: The hearing official must maintain a summary record of any hearing provided under this section.

claims.quote: The hearing official shall issue a written opinion stating his or her decision, as soon as practicable, but not later than sixty (60) days after the date on which the request for such hearing was received by the agency.
claims.summary: The hearing official shall issue a written opinion stating his or her decision within sixty (60) days after the date on which the request for such hearing was received by the agency.

claims.quote: The hearing official's decision will be the final agency action for the purposes of judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Act (5 U.S.C. 701 et seq. ).
claims.summary: The hearing official's decision will be the final agency action for the purposes of judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Act.

claims.quote: The hearing official shall issue a written opinion stating his or her decision, as soon as practicable, but not later than sixty (60) days after the date on which the request for such hearing was received by the agency. If an agency is unable to provide the debtor with a hearing and render a decision within 60 days after the receipt of the request for such hearing: (i) The agency may not issue a withholding order until the hearing is held and a decision rendered; or (ii) If the agency had previously issued a withholding order to the debtor's employer, the agency must suspend the withholding order beginning on the 61st day after the receipt of the hearing request and continuing until a hearing is held and a decision is rendered.
claims.summary: The agency may not issue a withholding order until the hearing is held and a decision is rendered if it is unable to provide the debtor with a hearing and render a decision within 60 days. If the agency had previously issued a withholding order, it must suspend the withholding order beginning on the 61st day after the receipt of the hearing request.

claims.quote: The written decision shall include: (i) A summary of the facts presented; (ii) The hearing official's findings, analysis and conclusions; and (iii) The terms of any repayment schedules, if applicable.
claims.summary: The written decision shall include a summary of the facts presented, the hearing official's findings, analysis, and conclusions, and the terms of any repayment schedules, if applicable.

claims.quote: In the absence of good cause shown, a debtor who fails to appear at a hearing scheduled pursuant to paragraph (f)(4) of this section will be deemed as not having timely filed a request for a hearing.
claims.summary: A debtor who fails to appear at a hearing scheduled pursuant to paragraph (f)(4) of this section will be deemed as not having timely filed a request for a hearing in the absence of good cause.

claims.quote: (1) Unless the agency receives information that the agency believes justifies a delay or cancellation of the withholding order, the agency should send, by first class mail, a withholding order to the debtor's employer: (i) Within 30 days after the debtor fails to make a timely request for a hearing ( i.e. , within 15 business days after the mailing of the notice described in paragraph (e)(1) of this section), or, (ii) If a timely request for a hearing is made by the debtor, within 30 days after a final decision is made by the agency to proceed with garnishment, or, (iii) As soon as reasonably possible thereafter.
claims.summary: The agency must send a withholding order to the debtor's employer within 30 days after the debtor fails to make a timely request for a hearing, or within 30 days after a final decision is made to proceed with garnishment, or as soon as reasonably possible thereafter.

claims.quote: (2) The withholding order sent to the employer under paragraph (g)(1) of this section shall be in a form prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury. The withholding order shall contain the signature of, or the image of the signature of, the head of the agency or his/her delegatee. The order shall contain only the information necessary for the employer to comply with the withholding order. Such information includes the debtor's name, address, and social security number, as well as instructions for withholding and information as to where payments should be sent.
claims.summary: The withholding order must be in a form prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury and must contain the signature of the head of the agency or his/her delegatee, along with the debtor's name, address, social security number, instructions for withholding, and information on where payments should be sent.

claims.quote: (3) The agency will retain evidence of service indicating the date of mailing of the order.
claims.summary: The agency must retain evidence of service indicating the date of mailing of the withholding order.

claims.quote: (h) Certification by employer. Along with the withholding order, the agency shall send to the employer a certification in a form prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury. The employer shall complete and return the certification to the agency within the time frame prescribed in the instructions to the form. The certification will address matters such as information about the debtor's employment status and disposable pay available for withholding.
claims.summary: The employer must complete and return a certification to the agency within the time frame prescribed in the instructions to the form, addressing matters such as the debtor's employment status and disposable pay available for withholding.

claims.quote: (i) Amounts withheld. (1) After receipt of the garnishment order issued under this section, the employer shall deduct from all disposable pay paid to the applicable debtor during each pay period the amount of garnishment described in paragraph (i)(2) of this section.
claims.summary: The employer must deduct from all disposable pay paid to the applicable debtor during each pay period the amount of garnishment described in paragraph (i)(2) of this section.

claims.quote: (2)(i) Subject to the provisions of paragraphs (i)(3) and (i)(4) of this section, the amount of garnishment shall be the lesser of: (A) The amount indicated on the garnishment order up to 15% of the debtor's disposable pay; or (B) The amount set forth in 15 U.S.C. 1673(a)(2) (Restriction on Garnishment). The amount set forth at 15 U.S.C. 1673(a)(2) is the amount by which a debtor's disposable pay exceeds an amount equivalent to thirty times the minimum wage. See 29 CFR 870.10.
claims.summary: The amount of garnishment shall be the lesser of (A) the amount indicated on the garnishment order up to 15% of the debtor's disposable pay, or (B) the amount set forth in 15 U.S.C. 1673(a)(2), which is the amount by which a debtor's disposable pay exceeds an amount equivalent to thirty times the minimum wage.

claims.quote: (3) When a debtor's pay is subject to withholding orders with priority the following shall apply: (i) Unless otherwise provided by Federal law, withholding orders issued under this section shall be paid in the amounts set forth under paragraph (i)(2) of this section and shall have priority over other withholding orders which are served later in time. Notwithstanding the foregoing, withholding orders for family support shall have priority over withholding orders issued under this section.
claims.summary: Withholding orders issued under this section shall be paid in the amounts set forth under paragraph (i)(2) of this section and shall have priority over other withholding orders served later in time, unless otherwise provided by Federal law. Withholding orders for family support shall have priority over withholding orders issued under this section.

claims.quote: (iii) If a debtor owes more than one debt to an agency, the agency may issue multiple withholding orders provided that the total amount garnished from the debtor's pay for such orders does not exceed the amount set forth in paragraph (i)(2) of this section. For purposes of this paragraph (i)(3)(iii), the term agency refers to the agency that is owed the debt.
claims.summary: If a debtor owes more than one debt to an agency, the agency may issue multiple withholding orders provided that the total amount garnished from the debtor's pay for such orders does not exceed the amount set forth in paragraph (i)(2) of this section.

claims.quote: (4) An amount greater than that set forth in paragraphs (i)(2) and (i)(3) of this section may be withheld upon the written consent of debtor.
claims.summary: An amount greater than that set forth in paragraphs (i)(2) and (i)(3) of this section may be withheld upon the written consent of debtor.

claims.quote: (5) The employer shall promptly pay to the agency all amounts withheld in accordance with the withholding order issued pursuant to this section.
claims.summary: The employer shall promptly pay to the agency all amounts withheld in accordance with the withholding order issued pursuant to this section.

claims.quote: (6) An employer shall not be required to vary its normal pay and disbursement cycles in order to comply with the withholding order.
claims.summary: An employer shall not be required to vary its normal pay and disbursement cycles in order to comply with the withholding order.

claims.quote: (7) Any assignment or allotment by an employee of his earnings shall be void to the extent it interferes with or prohibits execution of the withholding order issued under this section, except for any assignment or allotment made pursuant to a family support judgment or order.
claims.summary: Any assignment or allotment by an employee of his earnings shall be void to the extent it interferes with or prohibits execution of the withholding order issued under this section, except for any assignment or allotment made pursuant to a family support judgment or order.

claims.quote: (8) The employer shall withhold the appropriate amount from the debtor's wages for each pay period until the employer receives notification from the agency to discontinue wage withholding.
claims.summary: The employer shall withhold the appropriate amount from the debtor's wages for each pay period until the employer receives notification from the agency to discontinue wage withholding.

claims.quote: (j) Exclusions from garnishment. The agency may not garnish the wages of a debtor who it knows has been involuntarily separated from employment until the debtor has been reemployed continuously for at least 12 months. The debtor has the burden of informing the agency of the circumstances surrounding an involuntary separation from employment.
claims.summary: The agency may not garnish the wages of a debtor who it knows has been involuntarily separated from employment until the debtor has been reemployed continuously for at least 12 months. The debtor has the burden of informing the agency of the circumstances surrounding an involuntary separation from employment.

claims.quote: (k) Financial hardship. (1) A debtor whose wages are subject to a wage withholding order under this section, may, at any time, request a review by the agency of the amount garnished, based on materially changed circumstances such as disability, divorce, or catastrophic illness which result in financial hardship.
claims.summary: A debtor whose wages are subject to a wage withholding order under this section, may, at any time, request a review by the agency of the amount garnished, based on materially changed circumstances such as disability, divorce, or catastrophic illness which result in financial hardship.

claims.quote: (2) A debtor requesting a review under paragraph (k)(1) of this section shall submit the basis for claiming that the current amount of garnishment results in a financial hardship to the debtor, along with supporting documentation. Agencies shall consider any information submitted in accordance with procedures and standards established by the agency.
claims.summary: A debtor requesting a review under paragraph (k)(1) of this section shall submit the basis for claiming that the current amount of garnishment results in a financial hardship to the debtor, along with supporting documentation. Agencies shall consider any information submitted in accordance with procedures and standards established by the agency.

claims.quote: (3) If a financial hardship is found, the agency shall downwardly adjust, by an amount and for a period of time agreeable to the agency, the amount garnished to reflect the debtor's financial condition. The agency will notify the employer of any adjustments to the amounts to be withheld.
claims.summary: If a financial hardship is found, the agency shall downwardly adjust, by an amount and for a period of time agreeable to the agency, the amount garnished to reflect the debtor's financial condition. The agency will notify the employer of any adjustments to the amounts to be withheld.

claims.quote: (l) Ending garnishment. (1) Once the agency has fully recovered the amounts owed by the debtor, including interest, penalties, and administrative costs consistent with the FCCS, the agency shall send the debtor's employer notification to discontinue wage withholding.
claims.summary: Once the agency has fully recovered the amounts owed by the debtor, including interest, penalties, and administrative costs consistent with the FCCS, the agency shall send the debtor's employer notification to discontinue wage withholding.

claims.quote: (2) At least annually, an agency shall review its debtors' accounts to ensure that garnishment has been terminated for accounts that have been paid in full.
claims.summary: At least annually, an agency shall review its debtors' accounts to ensure that garnishment has been terminated for accounts that have been paid in full.

claims.quote: (m) Actions prohibited by the employer. An employer may not discharge, refuse to employ, or take disciplinary action against the debtor due to the issuance of a withholding order under this section.
claims.summary: An employer may not discharge, refuse to employ, or take disciplinary action against the debtor due to the issuance of a withholding order under this section.

claims.quote: (n) Refunds. (1) If a hearing official, at a hearing held pursuant to paragraph (f)(3) of this section, determines that a debt is not legally due and owing to the United States, the agency shall promptly refund any amount collected by means of administrative wage garnishment.
claims.summary: If a hearing official, at a hearing held pursuant to paragraph (f)(3) of this section, determines that a debt is not legally due and owing to the United States, the agency shall promptly refund any amount collected by means of administrative wage garnishment.

claims.quote: (o) Right of action. The agency may sue any employer for any amount that the employer fails to withhold from wages owed and payable to an employee in accordance with paragraphs (g) and (i) of this section.
claims.summary: The agency may sue any employer for any amount that the employer fails to withhold from wages owed and payable to an employee in accordance with paragraphs (g) and (i) of this section.

claims.quote: In any event, termination of the collection action will have been deemed to occur if the agency has not received any payments to satisfy the debt from the particular debtor whose wages were subject to garnishment, in whole or in part, for a period of one (1) year.
claims.summary: If no payments are received from the debtor for one year, the collection action is deemed terminated.

claims.quote: (1) A debt is considered eligible for transfer to the Cross-Servicing program only if it is past due and is legally enforceable.
claims.summary: A debt must be past due and legally enforceable to be eligible for transfer to the Cross-Servicing program.

claims.quote: (2) Except as set forth in paragraphs (c)(3) and (d) of this section, a creditor agency must transfer any eligible debt that is over $25 (or such other amount as Fiscal Service may determine) to the Cross-Servicing program by no later than 120 days delinquent if the creditor agency relies on the Cross-Servicing program to submit the transferred debts for centralized offset on the creditor agency's behalf or, otherwise, by no more than 18 than 180 days delinquent.
claims.summary: A creditor agency must transfer any eligible debt that is over $25 (or such other amount as Fiscal Service may determine) to the Cross-Servicing program by no later than 120 days delinquent if the creditor agency relies on the Cross-Servicing program to submit the transferred debts for centralized offset on the creditor agency's behalf or, otherwise, by no more than 180 days delinquent.

claims.quote: (3) If a final agency determination resulting from an administrative appeal or review process is not made until after the time specified in paragraph (c)(2) of this section, the creditor agency must transfer such debt to the Cross-Servicing program within 30 days after the date of the final decision.
claims.summary: If a final agency determination resulting from an administrative appeal or review process is not made until after the time specified in paragraph (c)(2) of this section, the creditor agency must transfer such debt to the Cross-Servicing program within 30 days after the date of the final decision.

claims.quote: (5) On behalf of the creditor agency, Fiscal Service will take appropriate action to collect or compromise the transferred debt, or to suspend or terminate collection action thereon. Appropriate action to collect a debt may include referral to another debt collection center, a private collection contractor, or the Department of Justice for litigation. The creditor agency must advise Fiscal Service, in writing, of any specific statutory or regulatory requirements pertaining to its debt and will agree, in writing, to a collection strategy, which includes parameters for entering into compromise and repayments agreements with debtors.
claims.summary: The creditor agency must advise Fiscal Service, in writing, of any specific statutory or regulatory requirements pertaining to its debt and will agree, in writing, to a collection strategy, which includes parameters for entering into compromise and repayments agreements with debtors.

claims.quote: (d)(1) A creditor agency is not required to transfer a debt to Fiscal Service pursuant to paragraph (c)(1) of this section only during such period of time that the debt: (i) Is in litigation or foreclosure as described in paragraph (d)(2) of this section; (ii) Is scheduled for sale as described in paragraph (d)(3) of this section; (iii) Is at a private collection contractor if the debt has been referred to a private collection contractor for a period of time determined by the Secretary; (iv) Is at a debt collection center if the debt has been referred to a Treasury-designated debt collection center in accordance with paragraph (f) of this section; (v) Is being collected by internal offset as described in paragraph (d)(4) of this section; (vi) Is being serviced and/or collected in accordance with applicable statutes and/or regulations by third parties, such as private lenders or guaranty agencies; or (vii) Is covered by an exemption granted by the Secretary as described in paragraph (d)(5) of this section.
claims.summary: A creditor agency is not required to transfer a debt to Fiscal Service pursuant to paragraph (c)(1) of this section only during such period of time that the debt is in litigation or foreclosure, scheduled for sale, at a private collection contractor, at a debt collection center, being collected by internal offset, being serviced and/or collected in accordance with applicable statutes and/or regulations by third parties, or covered by an exemption granted by the Secretary.

claims.quote: (2)(i) A debt is in litigation if: (A) The debt has been referred to the Attorney General for litigation by the creditor agency; or (B) The debt is the subject of proceedings pending in a court of competent jurisdiction, including bankruptcy proceedings, whether initiated by the creditor agency, the debtor, or any other party.
claims.summary: A debt is in litigation if the debt has been referred to the Attorney General for litigation by the creditor agency or if the debt is the subject of proceedings pending in a court of competent jurisdiction, including bankruptcy proceedings, whether initiated by the creditor agency, the debtor, or any other party.

claims.quote: (2)(ii) A debt is in foreclosure if: (A)( 1 ) Collateral securing the debt is the subject of judicial foreclosure proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction; or ( 2 ) Notice has been issued that collateral securing the debt will be foreclosed upon, liquidated, sold, or otherwise transferred pursuant to applicable law in a nonjudicial proceeding; and (B) The creditor agency anticipates that proceeds will be available from the liquidation of the collateral for application to the debt.
claims.summary: A debt is in foreclosure if collateral securing the debt is the subject of judicial foreclosure proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction, or notice has been issued that collateral securing the debt will be foreclosed upon, liquidated, sold, or otherwise transferred pursuant to applicable law in a nonjudicial proceeding, and the creditor agency anticipates that proceeds will be available from the liquidation of the collateral for application to the debt.

claims.quote: (3) A debt is scheduled for sale if: (i) The debt will be disposed of under an asset sales program within one (1) year after becoming eligible for sale; or (ii) The debt will be disposed of under an asset sales program and a schedule established by the creditor agency and approved by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.
claims.summary: A debt is scheduled for sale if the debt will be disposed of under an asset sales program within one (1) year after becoming eligible for sale, or if the debt will be disposed of under an asset sales program and a schedule established by the creditor agency and approved by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

claims.quote: (4) A debt is being collected by internal offset if a creditor agency expects the debt to be collected in full within three (3) years from the date of delinquency through the withholding of funds payable to the debtor by the creditor agency, or if the creditor agency has issued notice to the debtor of the creditor agency's intent to offset such funds.
claims.summary: A creditor agency must determine if a debt is being collected by internal offset based on the expectation of collection within three years or by issuing notice to the debtor.

claims.quote: (5) The Secretary may exempt classes of debt from mandatory referral.
claims.summary: The Secretary may exempt classes of debt from mandatory referral.

claims.quote: (f) Debt collection centers. claims.summary: A creditor agency may transfer debt less than 180 days delinquent to a Treasury-designated debt collection center with the consent of and in accordance with procedures established by Fiscal Service.

claims.quote: (g) Administrative offset. As described in paragraph (c) of this section, under the DCIA, agencies are required to transfer all debts over 180 days delinquent to Fiscal Service for purposes of debt collection ( i.e., cross-servicing). claims.summary: Agencies are required to transfer all debts over 180 days delinquent to Fiscal Service for debt collection and to notify the Secretary of all debts over 120 days delinquent for administrative offset.

claims.quote: Agencies relying on Fiscal Service to submit debts for administrative offset on the agency's behalf must transfer the debts to Fiscal Service no later than 120 days after the debts become delinquent in order to satisfy the 120-day notice requirement for purposes of administrative offset.

claims.quote: A creditor agency may refer any debt that is less than 180 days delinquent to Fiscal Service or, with the consent of Fiscal Service, to a Treasury-designated debt collection center for debt collection services.
claims.summary: A creditor agency may refer any debt that is less than 180 days delinquent to Fiscal Service or, with the consent of Fiscal Service, to a Treasury-designated debt collection center for debt collection services.

claims.quote: Before a debt may be transferred to Fiscal Service or another debt collection center, the head of the creditor agency or his or her delegate must certify, in writing, that the debts being transferred are valid, legally enforceable, and that there are no legal bars to collection.
claims.summary: The head of the creditor agency or his or her delegate must certify, in writing, that the debts being transferred are valid, legally enforceable, and that there are no legal bars to collection.

claims.quote: Creditor agencies must also certify that they have complied with all prerequisites to a particular collection action under the laws, regulations or policies applicable to the debt unless the creditor agency has requested, and Fiscal Service has agreed, to do so on the creditor agency's behalf.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies must certify that they have complied with all prerequisites to a particular collection action under the laws, regulations or policies applicable to the debt unless the creditor agency has requested, and Fiscal Service has agreed, to do so on the creditor agency's behalf.

claims.quote: The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service immediately of any change in the status of the legal enforceability of the debt, for example, if the creditor agency receives notice that the debtor has filed for bankruptcy protection.
claims.summary: The creditor agency shall notify Fiscal Service immediately of any change in the status of the legal enforceability of the debt, for example, if the creditor agency receives notice that the debtor has filed for bankruptcy protection.

claims.summary: Fiscal Service may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents under specific circumstances.

claims.quote: As required by the provisions of 31 U.S.C. 3720B, a person owing an outstanding nontax debt that is in delinquent status shall not be eligible for Federal financial assistance.
claims.summary: A person owing an outstanding nontax debt that is in delinquent status shall not be eligible for Federal financial assistance.

claims.quote: A person may be eligible for Federal financial assistance only after the delinquency is resolved in accordance with this section.
claims.summary: A person may be eligible for Federal financial assistance only after the delinquency is resolved in accordance with this section.

claims.quote: An agency may waive this eligibility requirement in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section.
claims.summary: An agency may waive this eligibility requirement in accordance with paragraph (g) of this section.

claims.quote: A creditor agency may obtain information concerning whether or not a person seeking Federal financial assistance owes a delinquent debt from, among other sources, credit reports, information contained on credit applications, and the Department of Housing and Urban Development's Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System (CAIVRS).
claims.summary: A creditor agency may obtain information concerning whether or not a person seeking Federal financial assistance owes a delinquent debt from, among other sources, credit reports, information contained on credit applications, and the Department of Housing and Urban Development's Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System (CAIVRS).

claims.quote: Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, a debt is in “delinquent status” for purposes of this section if the debt has not been paid within 90 days of the payment due date.
claims.summary: Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, a debt is in “delinquent status” for purposes of this section if the debt has not been paid within 90 days of the payment due date.

claims.quote: Unless otherwise prohibited, an agency may defer making a determination as to whether or not to extend credit until the appeal process is completed.
claims.summary: Unless otherwise prohibited, an agency may defer making a determination as to whether or not to extend credit until the appeal process is completed.

claims.quote: Unless the provisions of paragraph (d)(2) apply, a debt is in delinquent status even if the creditor agency has suspended or terminated collection activity with respect to such debt.
claims.summary: Unless the provisions of paragraph (d)(2) apply, a debt is in delinquent status even if the creditor agency has suspended or terminated collection activity with respect to such debt.

claims.quote: The creditor agency recommending an exemption for a class of debts will provide the Secretary with information about: (i) The nature of the program under which the delinquencies have arisen; (ii) The number, dollar amount, and age of the debts in the program for which exemption is recommended; (iii) The reasons why an exemption is justified, including why the granting of financial assistance to persons owing the type of debt for which exemption is requested would not be contrary to the Government's goal to reduce losses by requiring proper screening of potential borrowers; and, (iv) Other information the Secretary deems necessary to consider the exemption request.
claims.summary: The creditor agency recommending an exemption for a class of debts must provide the Secretary with information about the nature of the program, the number, dollar amount, and age of the debts, the reasons for the exemption, and other information the Secretary deems necessary.
